facts.raw_span: A 54-year-old fisherman with no significant medical history
complained of dyspnea, lethargy, severe generalized arthralgia, and mild confusion
Glasgow Coma Scale score of 14
bilateral joint pain worsened by movement without erythema or swelling
neurological, chest, cardiac, and abdominal examinations were otherwise unremarkable
Vital signs were blood pressure 90/60 mm Hg, pulse 95 bpm, respiratory rate 24/min, oxygen saturation 90% on room air, and temperature 36.6 °C
Wells pulmonary embolism score was 3
electrocardiogram was normal
Posterior–anterior chest radiography showed no abnormalities
white-cell count of 13 × 10^9/L
C-reactive protein 73 mg/L
arterial blood gas analysis demonstrated metabolic acidosis with pH 7.32, PCO2 28 mm Hg, HCO3– 15 mmol/L, and PO2 63 mm Hg
